Inbound email referencing Shadowbyt3$ extortion / leak negotiation AIActions on Objectives High
Alerts on inbound email mentioning the Shadowbyt3$ threat actor name, ransom amount, or known leak-site language combined with mega.nz URLs — the exact extortion-contact pattern the article describes (48-hour negotiation window, $2M demand). Catches the initial extortion approach to Nintendo and any subsequent victim outreach by the same actor. Rationale: Shadowbyt3$ is the named actor; '48 hours', '$2 million', 'extortion as a service', and 'Deleted Permanently' are direct quotes from the article's ransom note. The mega.nz URL join confirms it's the same leak-distribution pattern. Very low FP risk because the actor name is unique.
ATT&CKT1657 T1486
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / threat-intel team forwarding the BleepingComputer article internally for awareness
  • Vendor security-bulletin / SOC newsletter referencing the Nintendo breach
  • Legitimate inbound contact from journalists writing follow-up coverage
  • Phishing simulation that intentionally mimics extortion language for training
Suppression filter
| where SenderFromDomain !endswith "nintendo.com" and not (SenderFromAddress has_any ("@bleepingcomputer.com","@krebsonsecurity.com","securityalerts@"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the message, capture headers (especially Authentication-Results and Return-Path), verify the sender domain, and check whether the body contains a contact channel (Tox ID, qTox, Session, onion address, mega.nz link). Confirm whether the message reached an executive, legal, or comms inbox — those are the actor's typical targets. 2) Contain: quarantine the message tenant-wide via M365 Threat Explorer / soft-delete; alert legal + executive protection + comms before any reply is sent; do NOT engage with the threat actor. 3) Hunt: search EmailEvents for other inbound messages from the same SenderFromDomain or with the same mega.nz URL across the past 90 days; check whether any third-party HR/engagement SaaS (BambooHR, Culture Amp, Lattice, Officevibe) shows similar bulk-export or anomalous-geo sign-in activity — Shadowbyt3$ telegraphed 'more victims' so adjacent SaaS pivots are likely.
let ExtortionKeywords = dynamic(["Shadowbyt3","shadowbyt3","ShadowByt3$","shadow byt3"]);
let RansomLanguage = dynamic(["48 hours","48-hour","$2 million","2,000,000","extortion as a service","Deleted Permanently","leak site","data leak"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where Subject has_any (ExtortionKeywords)
    or Subject has_any (RansomLanguage)
| join kind=leftouter (
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any ("mega.nz","mega.io","mega.co.nz")
    | project NetworkMessageId, LeakUrl=Url
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
          RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation,
          LeakUrl, ThreatTypes
| order by Timestamp desc
let ExtortionKeywords = dynamic(["Shadowbyt3","shadowbyt3","ShadowByt3"]);
let RansomLanguage = dynamic(["48 hours","$2 million","2,000,000","extortion as a service","Deleted Permanently","data leak"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
| where Subject has_any (ExtortionKeywords) or Subject has_any (RansomLanguage)
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, Subject, Sender=tostring(Sender), Recipients=tostring(Recipients), MessageId=tostring(InternetMessageId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Close Encounters of the Human Kind
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos top-prevalence malware hash sweep — VID001.exe coinminer + f_000cd7.html (week of 2026-06-18) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match

Talos top-prevalence malware hash sweep — VID001.exe coinminer + f_000cd7.html (week of 2026-06-18) AIInstallation High
Hunts for execution or file-write activity matching the two complete SHA256 hashes Talos identified as most prevalent in their telemetry this week: a Win.Worm.Coinminer dropper observed as VID001.exe and a malicious HTML payload observed as f_000cd7.html (W32.C0AD494457-95.SBX.TG). Pure hash-IOC sweep — the article gives no behavioural context to pivot on. Rationale: Article is a Talos weekly newsletter — bulk is commentary / headlines with no IOCs. The only article-specific detectable content is the 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week' block, which lists two complete SHA256 + MD5 pairs (the third is truncated and unusable). Hashes are concrete, high-fidelity strings directly from the article. Filename hints (VID001.exe, f_000cd7.html) added to SPL/Sigma as supplemental selectors. No web corroboration performed — these are Talos's own first-party telemetry hashes and there's no campaign context to enrich.
ATT&CKT1496 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst workstations intentionally detonating samples (researcher sandbox VMs)
  • VirusTotal / threat-intel platform API workers caching the sample locally
  • SOC purple-team exercises replaying Talos prevalence-list IOCs to validate detection coverage
  • Endpoint backup/EDR quarantine restore operations re-materialising the file on disk
  • Pre-existing dormant infection from prior week being newly flagged as the hash is added to the watchlist
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "analyst" and DeviceName !has "malware-lab"
| join kind=leftanti (DeviceInfo | where MachineGroup has_any ("Threat Research", "Malware Analysis", "Sandbox")) on DeviceId
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full process tree around the hit — parent process, command line, write origin (FileOriginUrl on DeviceFileEvents). Confirm device is production (not analyst/sandbox) via DeviceInfo.DeviceCategory and machine group. Check Talos reputation page links and pivot the SHA256 in VT for current verdict. 2. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response / Falcon RTR if execution is confirmed (not just a stale file on disk). Kill the running process, quarantine the file, capture memory if coinminer behaviour suspected (high CPU, outbound to mining pools). 3. Hunt: pivot on the parent process / download URL and SHA256 of the dropper across the fleet to find sibling infections; query DeviceNetworkEvents for the host's outbound traffic in the hour around the file write for stratum+tcp:// mining-pool destinations (T1496) or unfamiliar C2 beacons; check DeviceRegistryEvents for Run-key persistence written by the same InitiatingProcessId.
let TalosTopHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe"]);
let ProcessHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in~ (TalosTopHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in~ (TalosTopHashes)
    | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceProcessEvents", DeviceName, AccountName,
              FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in~ (TalosTopHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in~ (TalosTopHashes)
    | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceFileEvents", DeviceName,
              AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
              ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentFileName=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              ParentCmd="";
union ProcessHits, FileHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TalosTopHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (TalosTopHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

F5 Patches Two Critical NGINX Open Source Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution

The Hacker News
2026-06-18 4 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

F5 has released security updates to address two critical security flaws in NGINX Open Source that could be exploited to achieve code execution on affected systems. The vulnerabilities are listed below - CVE-2026-42530 (CVSS v4 score: 9.2) - A use-after-free vulnerability in the ngx_http_v3_module that could be triggered by a remote unauthenticated attacker when NGINX Open Source is

CVEsCVE-2026-42530 CVE-2026-42055 CVE-2026-42945
ATT&CKT1190 T1555.003

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Inventory of hosts running NGINX versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-42530 / CVE-2026-42055 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] NGINX worker process spawning shell, scripting interpreter, or download utility
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
NGINX worker process spawning shell, scripting interpreter, or download utility AIExploitation High
Hunts for nginx master or worker processes spawning a shell, scripting interpreter, or networked download tool — the canonical post-exploitation footprint when CVE-2026-42530 (HTTP/3 QPACK use-after-free) or CVE-2026-42055 (HTTP/2 proxy heap overflow) results in code execution inside the nginx process tree. Article-specific to F5/NGINX RCE flaws rather than generic web-shell hunting. Rationale: Article names ngx_http_v3_module (QPACK UAF) and ngx_http_proxy_v2_module / ngx_http_grpc_module (heap overflow) as the RCE vehicles inside the nginx process — so any child process spawned BY nginx other than its own workers is a high-fidelity post-exploitation signal. Cross-checked with F5 advisory K000150000 and the prior CVE-2026-42945 (NGINX Rift) exploitation pattern noted in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000150000 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42530 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42055
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator-installed nginx wrappers (e.g. systemd ExecStartPre scripts) that legitimately call sh/bash for cert rotation
  • CI/CD config push agents that invoke `nginx -s reload` via a shell helper
  • Container init scripts where nginx is PID 1 and execs sh during graceful shutdown
  • Custom lua-resty modules shelling out to curl for upstream health checks
  • Certbot/acme.sh renewals that nginx invokes as a deploy-hook
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-s reload", "-s reopen", "-t") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("certbot", "acme.sh", "renew", "deploy-hook"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full nginx→child process tree, child command line, and SHA256. Confirm host runs an affected build (NGINX OSS 1.30.x/1.31.x, NGINX Plus R33-R37, Ingress Controller 3.5-5.5, App Protect 4.10-5.8, Gateway Fabric 1.3-2.6). Compare child process to host's documented nginx deploy hooks. 2) Contain: if child is not on the host's nginx-hook allowlist, isolate the host from the network, snapshot memory, and rotate any TLS keys / upstream credentials reachable from the nginx context. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP that opened the active HTTP/3 (UDP/443) or HTTP/2 session immediately preceding the spawn; sweep all internet-facing nginx hosts for the same parent→child tuple in the last 30 days; check `nginx -V` for `--with-http_v3_module` and audit `proxy_http_version 2` / `grpc_pass` / `ignore_invalid_headers off` / `large_client_header_buffers` in deployed configs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("nginx.exe", "nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "wget", "curl", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby", "nc", "ncat", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("nginx.exe", "nginx")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "wget", "curl", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby", "nc", "ncat", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: NGINX Worker Spawning Shell, Interpreter, or Download Utility
id: 3a1f8b4c-2e7d-4a92-9c3b-1f5e8d2a6b41
description: Detects nginx process spawning a shell, scripting interpreter, or download utility — likely post-exploitation of CVE-2026-42530 (HTTP/3 QPACK UAF) or CVE-2026-42055 (HTTP/2 proxy heap overflow).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/f5-patches-two-critical-nginx-open.html
  - https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000150000
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '/nginx'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/ruby'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Operator-driven nginx reload scripts that legitimately invoke shell wrappers
  - CI/CD or config-management agents reloading nginx via shell
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\nginx.exe OR *\NGINX.EXE OR */nginx) OR @process.parent.name:nginx) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR */bash OR */sh OR */dash OR */wget OR */curl OR */python OR */python3 OR */perl OR */nc OR */ncat OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^nginx(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|dash|zsh|wget|curl|python|python3|perl|ruby|nc|ncat|wscript|cscript)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| sort(field=_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="nginx.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="nginx") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","ruby","nc","ncat","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="nginx.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="nginx") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","ruby","nc","ncat","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Inventory of hosts running NGINX versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-42530 / CVE-2026-42055 AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces all managed devices reporting an NGINX OSS, NGINX Plus, NGINX Instance Manager, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, App Protect WAF/DoS, or F5 WAF for NGINX build in the affected version ranges. Drives the patch-now worklist instead of waiting for exploitation telemetry, since the article notes F5 NGINX CVE-2026-42945 (NGINX Rift) came under active exploitation within days of disclosure. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact affected product/version ranges (NGINX OSS 1.30.0-1.30.2 / 1.31.0-1.31.1, NGINX Plus 37.0.0-37.0.1 and R33-R36, Instance Manager 2.17-2.22, Ingress Controller 3.5-5.5, Gateway Fabric 1.3-2.6, App Protect WAF 4.10-5.8, App Protect DoS 4.3-4.7, F5 WAF for NGINX 5.9-5.13.1, F5 DoS for NGINX 4.9.0). Pivoting on DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities and SoftwareName='nginx*' surfaces them directly. Cross-checked against F5 K000150000. Cross-checked against: • https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000150000 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42530 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42055
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devices showing nginx via bundled container images that have already been replaced but TVM hasn't re-scanned
  • Lab/sandbox hosts intentionally kept on vulnerable builds for security research
  • NGINX Plus subscriptions where the fix-track (R36 P6) was applied without a version bump
  • Hosts running nginx behind a WAF that already mitigates the unauth attack surface
  • Embedded nginx in vendor appliances where the customer cannot patch directly
Response runbook
1) Triage: rank hits by IsInternetFacing=true, then by whether HTTP/3 (`--with-http_v3_module`) or HTTP/2 proxy directives (`proxy_http_version 2`, `grpc_pass`, `ignore_invalid_headers off`, `large_client_header_buffers >2MB`) are present in the deployed config. 2) Contain: for internet-facing vulnerable hosts that cannot be patched within 24h, apply F5's documented mitigations — disable HTTP/3 (`listen ... quic` removed) for CVE-2026-42530 and remove `ignore_invalid_headers off` or shrink `large_client_header_buffers` below 2 MB for CVE-2026-42055. 3) Hunt: cross-reference the inventory against egress logs to confirm whether ASLR is enforced on each host (ASLR-disabled or bypassable hosts are the actually-exploitable subset); run UC1 retroactively across all surfaced hosts for the last 30 days.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-42530", "CVE-2026-42055", "CVE-2026-42945")
   or (SoftwareName has_any ("nginx", "nginx plus", "nginx instance manager", "nginx ingress controller", "nginx gateway fabric", "nginx app protect", "f5 waf for nginx", "f5 dos for nginx"))
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d) | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-42530", "CVE-2026-42055", "CVE-2026-42945")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-42530", "CVE-2026-42055", "CVE-2026-42945")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
